martín: Martín (Antolínez) — a knight of Burgos, companion of the Cid, who provisions him on his exile and negotiates the loan from Raquel and Vidas
antolínez: Antolínez — surname of Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese knight who aids the Cid
burgalés: burgalés — a man of Burgos (noun/adj.; el Burgalés, an epithet of Martín Antolínez)
conplido: conplido — complete, accomplished (past part. used as adj.; = cumplido, a term of praise)
abástales: abastar + les — he supplies them (abasta, present 3rd sg. of abastar 'to supply, provide', + enclitic les)
vino: vino — wine (noun); also venir — he came (strong preterite 3rd sg.; por en vino a aquesto, 'that is how he came to this pass')
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
conducho: conducho — provisions, victuals (Latin conductus; covers everything an army eats)
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished')
bastidos: bastir — furnished, equipped (past part. masc. pl., still agreeing with its object, los … bastidos)
pagós: pagar + se — he was pleased, was satisfied (pagó + -s(e): -se shrinks to -s after a stressed vowel; = pagóse)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira')
odredes: oír — you will hear (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = oiréis; the minstrel's aside to his listeners)
dicho: dezir — said (past part.; a dicho = ha dicho, 'he has said')
canpeador: Campeador — spelling variant with n for m (copyist's spelling) of Campeador, the Cid's epithet
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour'
fostes: seer — you were (archaic 2nd pl. preterite of ser, used respectfully to one person; = fuestes)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
yagamos: yazer — let us lie down, let us spend the night (present subjunctive/hortative 1st pl.; Latin iacere)
vayámosnos: ir + nos — let us go away (hortative vayamos + reflexive enclitic nos, the stem-final -s retained before the pronoun; = vayámonos)
matino: matino — morning (= la mañana; al matino 'in the morning')
seré: seer — I shall be (future 1st sg. of ser)
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
ira: ira — wrath; en ira del rey = to be formally cast into the king's disgrace and exile, a legal idiom, not a mere figure of speech
alffons: Alfonso — Alfonso VI, king of Castile and León (copyist's shortened spelling, cf. alfons, alfonsso)
metido: meter — put, cast (past part.; seré metido = 'I shall be put/cast')
vusco: vusco — you (old fused form, con vusco = con vos, 'with you'; cf. convusco)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?')
çerca: çerca — near; here adverbial, çerca o tarde = 'sooner or later' (= cerca)
querer: querer — to want, wish (infinitive; head of the split future querer m'a = me querrá, 'he will want me')
m: me — me, to me (elided form of me before a vowel, querer m'a = me querrá)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto)
preçio: preçiar — I value, prize (present 1st sg.; = aprecio)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
figo: figo — fig (= higo); non preçiar un figo, 'not to value at a fig', an idiom of contempt for something worthless
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
lança: lança — lance (= lanza); ardida lança, 'bold lance', stands for the bold man who wields it
doblar: doblar — to double (infinitive; split future doblar vos he = os doblaré)
soldada: soldada — wages, pay (of a retained man; from sueldo)
espeso: espender — spent (past part.; = gastado; Latin expendere)
veedes: veer — you see (2nd pl. present, old -edes ending; = veis)
trayo: traer — I carry, bring (present 1st sg.; = traigo)
huebos: huebos — need (Latin opus); huebos (me) ser/aver = 'to have need (of)'
serié: seer — it would be (conditional 3rd sg.; = sería)
compaña: conpaña — company, retinue (= compañía; spelling variant with m of conpaña)
fer: fazer — to do, make (short infinitive form; = hacer; fer lo he = lo haré, split future)
avrié: aver — there would be, he/it would have (conditional 3rd sg.; = habría)
bastir: bastir — to build, rig up, equip (the verb for Martín Antolínez's honest provisioning at v. 68, now used of the counterfeit chests)
inchámoslas: inchir + las — let us fill them (hortative inchamos + enclitic las; inchir = hinchir 'to fill', Latin implere)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena)
guadalmeçí: guadalmeçí — tooled, gilded leather of the costliest kind (Arabic loan, from Ghadāmes; cf. guadameçís)
enclaveadas: enclavear — studded, nailed (past part. fem. pl.; = enclavadas)
guadameçís: guadalmeçí — gilded leather (spelling variant without l, the same word as guadalmeçí)
vermejos: vermejo — bright red, crimson (masc. pl.; = bermejo)
raquel: Raquel — one of the two Jewish moneylenders of Burgos who take the pawned chests
vidas: Vidas — the other of the two Jewish moneylenders of Burgos, partner of Raquel
vayádesme: ir + me — go for me (vayades, 2nd pl. imperative/subjunctive of ir, old -ades ending, + enclitic me)
compra: conpra — buying, purchase (spelling variant with m of conpra)
ayrado: ayrar — angered, placed in disgrace (past part.; = airado; el rey me a ayrado, 'the king has turned his wrath on me', the legal condition of ira)
aver: aver — wealth, property, goods (noun use of aver, beside aver the verb 'to have')
enpeñar: enpeñar — to pledge, pawn (infinitive; = empeñar; split future enpeñar gelo he = se lo empeñaré)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
fore: seer — it may be (future subjunctive 3rd sg. of ser; = fuere)
guisado: guisar — fitting, reasonable, right (past part. used as adj.)
lieven: llevar — let them carry (present subjunctive 3rd pl.; = lleven)
cristianos: cristiano — Christian(s) (masc. pl.); moros nin cristianos / cristianos alone idiomatically = 'anyone at all'
véalo: veer + lo — may he (the Creator) see it (present subjunctive vea + enclitic lo)
santos: santo — saint (masc. pl.); los sos santos 'his saints'
fago: fazer — I do, make (present 1st sg.; = hago)
detardava: detardar — was delaying (imperfect 3rd sg.; = tardaba, se retrasaba)
passó: passar — he passed, crossed (preterite 3rd sg.; = pasó)
castiello: castiello — castle (= castillo; here the castle quarter of Burgos)
demandava: demandar — he was asking after, inquiring for (imperfect 3rd sg.)
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one'
ganados: ganar — gained, earned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with its object, as with ovo bastidos; avien ganados = habían ganado)
guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of'
menbrado: menbrado — prudent, shrewd (lit. 'mindful', from membrar 'to bear in mind')
caros: caro — dear, beloved (masc. pl.; not 'expensive' here)
poridad: poridad — secrecy, privacy, confidence (= puridad); en poridad 'in confidence'
fablar: fablar — to speak (infinitive; = hablar, note f-)
querría: querer — I would like, would want (conditional 1st sg.)
detardan: detardar — they delay (present 3rd pl.; cf. detardava)
apartaron: apartar — they drew aside, withdrew (preterite 3rd pl., reflexive se apartaron)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding
descubrades: descubrir — you (may) reveal, betray (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades ending; = descubráis)
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
siempre: siempre — always, forever; por siempre 'for ever'
faré: fazer — I shall make (future 1st sg.; = haré)
seades: seer — you may be (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades ending; = seáis)
menguados: menguado — diminished, in want, needy (past part./adj. pl.)
parias: paria — tribute paid by the Muslim taifa kingdoms to Castile (pl.)
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something')
entrado: entrar — entered, gone in (past part.; f[o] entrado = 'had gone in', a ser + participle periphrasis)
priso: prender — he took (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = prendió, tomó)
sobejanos: sobejano — excessive, abundant beyond measure (masc. pl. adj.)
retovo: retener — he kept back, retained (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = retuvo)
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth
esmerado: esmerar — refined, assayed, purified (past part.; of gold, the costliest kind)
dexado: dexar — left, left behind (past part.; = dejado)
palaçios: palaçio — great hall, manor-house (pl.; = palacio, here not 'royal palace')
aquellas: aquel — those (fem. pl.; here referring back to the chests)
levar: levar — to carry, carry off (= llevar)
sinon: sinon — if not, otherwise, but rather (= sino, si no)
ventado: ventar — scented out, got wind of (past part.; a hunting word, 'nosed out')
dexar: dexar — to leave (infinitive; = dejar; split future dexar las ha = las dejará)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping'
prestalde: prestar + le — lend to him! (imperative prestad + enclitic le, with Old Spanish metathesis -dl- > -ld-; = prestadle)
sea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
metedlas: meter + las — put them! (imperative meted + enclitic las)
salvo: salvo — safety, safe-keeping (noun; en vuestro salvo 'in your safe keeping')
fedes: fe — pledged faiths (Pidal's restored older plural of fe 'faith, troth'; meted las fedes = 'pledge your faith')
catedes: catar — you may look into, inspect (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -edes ending; catar here = 'to look into, inspect')
seiense: seer + se — they were sitting (themselves) (seíen + enclitic se, periphrastic with gerund: seiense consejando = 'sat taking counsel')
gañado: ganar — gained, earned (past part.; = ganado, here spelled with ñ)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien)
monedado: monedar — coined, minted (past part. used as adj.; aver monedado = 'wealth in coin')
prendámoslas: prender + las — let us take them (hortative prendamos + enclitic las)
metamos: meter — let us put (hortative subjunctive 1st pl.)
dezidnos: dezir + nos — tell us! (imperative dezid + enclitic nos; = decidnos)
pagado: pagar — satisfied, pleased; also paid (past part.; será pagado = 'he will be content with')
respuso: responder — he answered (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = respondió)
myo: mio — my (unstressed possessive, variant spelling of mio)
ssea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; spelling variant of sea)
aguisado: guisar — fitting, reasonable (past part. used as adj.; variant of guisado)
pedir: pedir — to ask, request (infinitive; split future pedir vos a = os pedirá)
acógensele: acoger + se + le — they gather to him, flock to him (acógense + enclitic le, reflexive and dative both glued to the verb)
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
menester: menester — need; a menester = ha menester, 'he has need of'
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
gelos: ge + los — them to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + los; = se los)
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
vedes: veer — you see (2nd pl. present, old -edes ending; = veis)
entra: entrar — it comes in, enters (present 3rd sg.)
pressurado: apresurar — hurried, pressed for time (past part.; = apresurado)
dedes: dar — you may give (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = deis)
faze: fazer — is done, is made (present 3rd sg.; = hace)
desso: desso — of that, with that (= de eso)
pago: pagar — I am content, satisfied (present 1st sg., reflexive me pago)
tred: trer/traer — come! come along! (2nd pl. imperative, old form, intransitive sense of traer; = venid)
contado: contar — renowned, esteemed (past part. used as a standing epithet of the Campeador)
meterlas: meter + las — to put them (infinitive meter + enclitic las)
sepan: saber — may know, should know (present subjunctive 3rd pl.)
pagamos: pagar — we are content, satisfied (present 1st pl., reflexive nos pagamos)
archas: arca — chest, coffer (pl.; spelling variant with ch of arcas)
aduchas: aducir — brought (irregular past part. fem. pl. of aducir)
prendet: prender — take! (2nd pl. imperative, variant spelling of prended)
seyesçientos: seysçientos — six hundred (spelling variant of seysçientos/seiscientos)
caualgó: cavalgar — he rode, mounted (preterite 3rd sg.; copyist's u-for-v spelling of cavalgó; = cabalgó)
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly'
ventassen: ventar — should scent out, get wind of (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl.; hunting word)
nado: nacer — born (past part.; = nacido); omne nado, 'man born', an all-inclusive idiom like moros nin cristianos
afévoslos: afé + vos + los — here/behold them for you (afé, the poem's pointing word, origin disputed, perhaps Arabic hā 'behold', + two enclitic pronouns vos + los)
besáronle: besar + le — they kissed him (preterite besaron + enclitic le; besar las manos, the formal courtesy owed to a lord)
sonrrisós: sonrreír + se — he smiled (sonrrisó + -s(e); = sonrrisóse, -se reduced to -s after a stressed vowel)
avédesme: aver + me — you-have … me (avedes, 2nd pl. present of aver, old -edes ending, + enclitic me; = habéis + me, perfect auxiliary; avédesme olbidado = 'you have forgotten me', a host's mock-reproach)
exco: exir — I go out, I leave (present 1st sg. of exir; = salgo; cf. exien)
quem: que + me — that to me (= que me, worn down to a single consonant, cf. nol)
semeja: semejar — it seems, appears (present 3rd sg.; = parece)
avredes: aver — you will have (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = habréis)
mientra: mientra — while, as long as (= mientras)
vivades: vivir — you may live (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades ending; = viváis)
seredes: seer — you will be (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = seréis)
pleyto: pleyto — covenant, agreed terms, bargain (Latin placitum; = pleito)
parado: parar — settled, arranged (past part.; el pleyto a parado = 'has settled the agreement')
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas)
gelas: ge + las — them for/to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + las; = se las)
guardarien: guardar — they would guard (conditional 3rd pl.; = guardarían)
fasta: fasta — until, as far as (= hasta)
assil: assí + le — thus to him (assí + enclitic l(e))
dieran: dar — they had given (pluperfect in -ra; = habían dado)
fed: fe — pledged faith, troth (Pidal's restored older form of fe)
auien: aver — they had (imperfect 3rd pl., copyist's u-for-v spelling; = avían/habían)
catassen: catar — they should look into, inspect (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl.)
fossen: seer — they should be (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl. of ser, Pidal's older form; = fuesen; cf. fosse)
dinero: dinero — penny (a small coin, the unit of smallest denomination)
malo: malo — bad; un dinero malo, 'one bad penny' — a debased coin, naming the smallest thing worth mentioning
carguen: cargar — let them load (present subjunctive used as imperative, 3rd pl.)
levaldas: levar + las — carry them off! (imperative levad + enclitic las, with metathesis -dl- > -ld-; = llevadlas)
ponedlas: poner + las — put them! (imperative poned + enclitic las)
convusco: con + vusco — with you (fused form; cf. con vusco, v. 75)
adugamos: aducir — let us bring, fetch (hortative subjunctive 1st pl.)
mover: mover — to move, set out (infinitive; a mover [h]a = ha de mover, 'he has to set out', aver a + infinitive for obligation)
cante: cantar — may crow, may sing (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
gallo: gallo — cock, rooster; ante que cante el gallo, 'before the cock crows'
cargar: cargar — to load; al cargar de las arcas, 'at the loading of the chests'
veriedes: veer — you would have seen (conditional 2nd pl.; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
podien: poder — they could, were able (imperfect 3rd pl.; = podían)
somo: somo — top, summit; en somo 'on top'
maguer: maguer — although (a rare word, of Greek origin)
grádanse: gradar + se — they rejoice, take pleasure (reflexive present 3rd pl.; = se alegran)
monedados: monedar — coined, minted (past part. pl.; cf. monedado sg.)
visquiessen: vivir — they might live (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl., strong irregular form; = viviesen)
refechos: refazer — restored, set up again, made rich (past part. pl.)

__broaden__.a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado)
__broaden__.e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
__broaden__.conpra: conpra — buying, purchase (= compra) · also comprar — he/she buys (present 3rd sg.; = compra), as in non lo conpra, 'he does not buy it'
__broaden__.grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had')
__broaden__.i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
__broaden__.qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied')
__broaden__.cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year')
